overall_summary: Most self-respect and emotional shorts have extremely low views (0-41 range), except for an outlier about mothers ('Maa Shayari') which hit 196 views. Since sample size and engagement are overall very low and volatile, confidence is low, indicating a need for a controlled exploration strategy combining the core emotional niche with a fresh angle.

winning_patterns.evidence: The video about Mother ('माँ जब पूछती है...') achieved 196 views and 17 likes, vastly outperforming romantic/self-respect chat deletion tropes.
winning_patterns.action: Test more family or foundational emotional bonds instead of solely focusing on digital breakup/self-respect tropes.

winning_patterns.evidence: Self-respect hooks involving specific phone actions like removing names from lists or changing settings scored slightly higher (30-41 views) compared to generic overthinking.
winning_patterns.action: Keep grounded in hyper-specific physical or digital habits if sticking to the romance/self-respect genre.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'रात के दो बजे' and 'रात के ख्याल' got very low views (6-13 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid abstract late-night rambling; anchor text in concrete daily scenarios.

weak_patterns.evidence: Too many consecutive variations of blocking, unpinning chats, and deleting archives have resulted in audience fatigue and near-zero views on recent uploads.
weak_patterns.action: Pause the repetitive WhatsApp/chat-deletion template and introduce fresh emotional contexts.
